title: How to Choose a Web Development Company: 12 Questions to Ask Before You Sign
summary: A checklist to choose the right web development company or agency anywhere in the world: 12 questions on process, SEO, ownership, pricing and support, plus red flags to avoid.
body:
Choosing a web development company is a big decision. The right partner builds a website or app that brings clients for years. The wrong one leaves you with delays, hidden costs and a site you cannot update or move.

Because you can now work with agencies anywhere in the world, the choice is wider than ever. These 12 questions help you compare providers on what really matters.

## Before you start: know what you need

Write down your goal (leads, sales, bookings, credibility), the main features, your budget range and your deadline. A clear brief is the best way to get comparable quotes.

## 12 questions to ask

### 1. Can you show similar projects?
Ask for live examples in your industry or of similar complexity, and what results they achieved.

### 2. Who will actually work on my project?
Know whether the work is done in-house, by freelancers or outsourced, and who your single point of contact is.

### 3. What is your process?
A good company explains its steps: discovery, design approval, development, testing, launch and support.

### 4. How do you handle SEO?
Your site should launch with technical SEO built in: speed, structure, tags, structured data and a sitemap. If SEO is "an extra for later", be careful.

### 5. How fast will the site be on mobile?
Most visits come from phones. Ask for target speed scores and examples of fast sites they built.

### 6. Will I own the site and the code?
You should own your domain, content and code, with admin access. Avoid contracts that lock your site to one provider.

### 7. Can I update content myself?
Ask for a demo of the admin area and whether training is included.

### 8. What exactly is included in the price?
Get a written scope: pages, features, revisions, content, hosting and launch. Ask what counts as extra work.

### 9. What happens after launch?
Clarify maintenance, security updates, backups and response times, and their monthly cost.

### 10. How do you communicate?
For remote projects, agree on channels (video calls, WhatsApp, e-mail), language and the frequency of updates.

### 11. How do you measure success?
Good partners talk about leads, conversions and traffic, not only about design.

### 12. Can you help with more than the website?
Mobile apps, automation, AI chatbots and marketing often come next. One partner who understands the whole picture saves time and money.

## Red flags to avoid

- A price given without understanding your needs.
- No examples or references.
- Vague answers on ownership and hosting.
- No mention of SEO, speed or mobile.
- Pressure to sign quickly.

## Local or remote agency?

Remote agencies can offer more expertise for the same budget, as long as communication is clear. Look for a partner who works in your language, overlaps with your time zone for a few hours a day and gives you regular updates.
